- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 5.0), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 2x prior peak or use 3-day moving average to dampen.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) within 3 days, model overreacts; apply downward bias of 15–25% to forecast if sentiment drops below 0.33.
- Model underestimates true price volatility in early horizon (first 5–7 days); increase forecast by 10–20% for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- Mean reversion is strong in late horizon (last 5–7 days); if forecast is >20% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 15–30%.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model tends to overfit short-term swings; smooth forecast with 3-day exponential moving average.
